name: London
intro: London lots tend to be deeper than they are wide, which suits a half court behind the garage or a pickleball court along the back fence.
local: In established neighbourhoods like Byron, Oakridge and Old North, a 25 by 20 or 30 by 25 foot half court is usually the largest pad that fits beside a patio. Newer subdivisions and the rural edges around Lambeth, Arva and Komoka often have space for a 60 by 30 multi-game pad.
Southwestern Ontario gets real freeze-thaw. A court that floats on the slab rather than being painted onto it does not peel when the concrete moves a little over winter.
Kits are quoted with freight to London and the surrounding area, including St. Thomas, Strathroy and Woodstock.

name: Kitchener-Waterloo
intro: From Doon to Laurelwood, Waterloo Region backyards are a natural fit for a compact half court or a 52 by 28 pickleball kit.
local: Most suburban lots in Kitchener, Waterloo and Cambridge can take a 25 by 25 or 30 by 25 foot pad once setbacks are respected. Country properties in Wilmot, Woolwich and North Dumfries have room for full pickleball and multi-game courts.
If you are adding a pad, check the lot coverage rules for your municipality before the concrete truck is booked. Each of the three cities and four townships sets its own limits.
Freight quotes cover Kitchener, Waterloo, Cambridge, Guelph and the townships.

name: Hamilton
intro: On the Mountain, in Ancaster or out toward Flamborough, a tile court turns a plain concrete pad into the most used part of the yard.
local: City lots on the Mountain and in Stoney Creek generally suit a starter or classic half court. Ancaster, Dundas and rural Flamborough and Glanbrook properties can carry a 30 by 60 pickleball or multi-game pad.
Have an old asphalt pad or a disused tennis court? If it is firm and fairly flat, tile can go straight over it and save the cost of new concrete.
Kits are quoted delivered to Hamilton, Burlington, Grimsby and the Niagara Peninsula.

name: Winnipeg
intro: Winnipeg has some of the widest temperature swings of any Canadian city. A floating tile surface is built to move with them.
local: Plastic expands in July heat and shrinks in a January cold snap. Your layout plan shows a small gap to leave around the court edge so the surface can move freely through a Manitoba year.

Larger lots in Charleswood, St. Vital and the surrounding municipalities of Headingley, East St. Paul and Springfield suit pickleball and multi-game pads. In the city, a half court on the garage apron is the simplest project.
Freight quotes cover Winnipeg and southern Manitoba, including Steinbach, Selkirk and Brandon.

name: Halifax
intro: Fog, drizzle and salt air are part of life in Halifax. An open-grid tile court drains through instead of holding puddles.
local: Coastal weather means courts are wet more often than not. Perforated tiles let water pass to the pad below so the playing surface is usable sooner after rain.
Lots in Bedford, Hammonds Plains, Fall River and along the Eastern Shore often have room for a full 60 by 30 pad. On the peninsula and in Dartmouth, compact half courts are the practical choice.
Kits are quoted with freight to Halifax Regional Municipality and the rest of Nova Scotia, and to New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island on request.
